asr.full_text: Hello, it is Elena Apalkava with you today and in this short video we will see how to send our Euros from trading account to the exchange to buy tokens. As you know 40 percent of every week our cheque goes to trading account and we can buy one coins or tokens. Now I want to buy tokens and I will show you how to do this. So we enter trading account section. We want to buy tokens by 0.228 euros. So we divide 2.021 euros by today's price of tokens and buy buy tokens. We get to this site and we press bid to buy tokens. So we enter here the number of tokens which we can buy for this price, yes, two thousand twenty and ninety-nine Euros, yes, and we can see our order was accepted and this quantitative of This quantity of tokens will go to this end. Now come back to our Dashboard. Money is still there but don't worry, it will get to this section and the Bought amount of tokens will be added to the amount of the tokens which you already have bought. Thank you very much. Bye Bye. Thank you very much! Thank you very much and see you in next video, have a great day!

textual.observation: The source presents a procedure to send euros from a trading account to an exchange and place a bid to buy tokens, while stating that 40 percent of a weekly cheque goes to the trading account and can be used to buy tokens from a mandatory account.

textual.context: Instructional demonstration of a token-purchase procedure; whether it is broader promotion or discussion is unclear from these records.
textual.potential_relevance: The source links a claimed recurring money allocation and a mandatory-account condition to a requested transfer and token purchase, creating a relationship that may require later context assessment.
textual.limitations: The records do not establish whether the cheque, account, exchange, tokens, or transaction are genuine, whether any money was lost, or whether viewers are being solicited beyond the demonstrated procedure.

visual.observation: A OneCoin-branded account dashboard visibly shows multiple bonus and reward balances, including “BONUS EARNED THIS WEEK,” “TOTAL BONUS EARNED,” “ONE LIFE POINTS,” and a countdown labeled “UNTIL NEXT BONUS ROUND.” Other sampled screens show token purchasing and trading-account activity, including transaction-history entries for matching and online bonuses and an automatic token purchase from mandatory accounts.
visual.context: Visible account, exchange, and order-entry interfaces; the relationship between displayed bonuses and token purchasing/trading is shown, but the surrounding promotional or explanatory context is unclear.
visual.potential_relevance: The frames connect displayed bonus/reward returns with token purchasing, trading, and an automatic purchase entry, which is a task-relevant reward-to-financial-action relationship meriting review.
visual.limitations: These sampled frames cannot establish whether any transaction was completed, whether the bonuses were actually redeemable, what terms applied outside the visible screens, or whether the displayed balances represented real funds.

visual.observation: A buy-order dialog visibly requests a token quantity and a transaction password before placing an order; the screen shows a stated token price of 0.228 EUR and a transaction value of 20.28 EUR, while the surrounding interface displays token and bonus-related balances.
visual.context: This appears to be an account trading/order interface. In one sampled frame, the password field is populated with masked characters and a browser alert is visible.
visual.potential_relevance: The interface links a financial purchase and credential entry to the platform’s token and bonus system, creating a concrete payment-plus-authentication flow for review.
visual.limitations: The frames cannot establish whether the order was submitted or accepted, whether the password was valid, who controlled the account, or what happened after the alert was dismissed.

textual_context_notes.observation: The speaker reassures viewers after describing money remaining in the account and being added to the purchased-token amount.

evidence.quote: Money is still there but don't worry, it will get to this section and the Bought amount of tokens will be added to the amount of the tokens which you already have bought

visual_context_notes.observation: The sampled sequence shows a OneCoin-branded dashboard, trading account, exchange chart, and buy-order interface rather than an explicitly labeled warning, report, parody, or educational demonstration.
A browser alert is visible over the buy-order screen, and the displayed message begins with a page URL using the onecoin.eu domain; the full message and outcome are not observable.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because it actively instructs viewers to move euros into a mandatory account and purchase OneCoin tokens as a way to start mining them. The presentation promotes participation in a token-and-mining scheme through a concrete purchase flow, including entering an order and transaction password, rather than warning about or analyzing the offer.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: S04 fits because the video links purchasing token participation through a mandatory account with starting or increasing token mining, and demonstrates the payment/order process used to participate.

evidence.observation: The description presents buying OneCoin tokens from a mandatory account as the participation step for starting mining.
